title: Quality assurance and project assurance
blurb: Explain quality assurance as an independent business function and tell it apart from project assurance, which acts for the project board.
question: Which statement about project assurance is correct?

teach.body: Formally: quality assurance is a planned and systematic activity that provides confidence that products will meet their defined quality specifications when tested under quality control. In plain English: someone outside the project looks at how the project checks its products and asks, 'Will these checks really show whether the products are good enough?' It is the third quality element, alongside quality planning and quality control.

teach.caption: Quality assurance is managed outside the project management team; project assurance belongs to the board inside the project.

teach.h: Independent of the project management team
teach.body: Quality assurance is typically performed at business or programme level, for example by part of the business's quality management system. It focuses on whether the project's quality control measures are appropriate for assessing products against their quality specifications. Because it is independent of the whole project management team, it can challenge the project's own checks without a conflict of interest.

Project assurance is the project board's responsibility and confirms that the project is being conducted correctly. It is independent of the project manager but NOT of the project. Each board member is accountable for assurance of their interest (business, user, supplier); the board decides how it is done, using board members, people appointed from the business, or external specialists. The project manager, project team members and project support cannot perform it.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a payroll system upgrade
teach.body: Ashcombe Building Society is upgrading its payroll system. The project board asks finance manager Ruth Keane to provide business assurance and an HR analyst, Omar Siddiqui, to provide user assurance; both report to board members. Separately, the society's quality and compliance team, which sits outside the project, audits the project's test plans and confirms they are fit to prove the system meets its specifications. The project manager, Hannah Doyle, proposed doing the assurance herself to save time; the board declined.

teach.text: Classic trap: project assurance is NOT quality assurance. Project assurance is the board's responsibility and is independent of the project manager but part of the project. Quality assurance is a business or programme function independent of the whole project management team. And neither can be carried out by the project manager or project support.

items: Quality assurance: planned, systematic confidence that products will meet specifications under quality control.
Quality assurance is managed outside the project management team, typically by the business.
It checks that the project's quality control measures are appropriate.
Project assurance: board's responsibility; independent of the PM, not of the project.
The PM, project team members and project support cannot do project assurance.

summary: You can now define quality assurance and explain why it sits outside the project management team. You can also contrast it with project assurance, which acts for the board and is independent of the project manager but not of the project.

A.q: Which statement about project assurance is correct?
options: It is independent of the project manager but not of the project
It is a business function outside the project management team
It is carried out by project support on behalf of the PM
It defines the quality specifications for each product
A.why: Project assurance is the project board's responsibility and is independent of the project manager but not of the project (manual 8.2.3).

whyNot.1: This describes quality assurance, which is managed outside the project management team.
whyNot.2: Project support cannot perform project assurance; the two must be kept separate.
whyNot.3: Quality specifications are captured in quality planning and recorded in product descriptions.

A.q: Who typically carries out quality assurance?
options: The team managers delivering the products
The project manager, assisted by project support
A function of the business, outside the project team
The senior supplier as a member of the board
A.why: Quality assurance is typically performed by a business or programme function, independent of the project management team (manual 8.2.3).

whyNot.0: Team managers carry out quality control on their products, not quality assurance.
whyNot.1: The PM and support are part of the project management team, so they are not independent.
whyNot.3: Board members are part of the project management team; their assurance role is project assurance.

A.q: What does quality assurance focus on?
options: Whether the business case is still justified
Whether the project's quality controls are appropriate
Whether stage tolerances will be exceeded
Whether the team plan matches the stage plan
A.why: Quality assurance focuses on ensuring the project's quality control measures are appropriate to assess products against their quality specifications.

whyNot.0: Continued justification is reviewed by the board through the business case.
whyNot.2: Forecasting tolerance breaches is part of the progress practice.
whyNot.3: Checking plans is the work of the PM and project assurance, not quality assurance.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. Quality assurance is part of the project board's responsibilities.
2. Project assurance can be provided by people appointed from the business.
3. Quality assurance is managed independently of the project management team.
4. The project manager may carry out project assurance on a small project.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 4
3 and 4
2 and 3
B.why: The board may use people appointed from the business for project assurance (2), and quality assurance is managed outside the project management team (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 is false: project assurance, not quality assurance, is the board's responsibility.
whyNot.1: Both are false: quality assurance is a business function, and the PM cannot do project assurance.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: the PM cannot carry out project assurance on any size of project.

B.q: A project manager offers to provide user assurance to reduce costs. Why is this inappropriate?
options: Project assurance must be independent of the project manager
User assurance is the responsibility of the business layer
Assurance roles must be filled by external consultants
The senior user must perform all user assurance personally
B.why: Project assurance is independent of the project manager, so the PM cannot perform it.

whyNot.1: The board decides how assurance is provided; it may use board members, business appointees or external people.
whyNot.2: External people are one option, not a requirement.
whyNot.3: The senior user may delegate assurance work, though accountability stays with them.

B.q: A council's internal audit team, independent of the project, reviews whether the project's testing will prove products meet their specifications. What is this?
options: Project assurance
Quality control
Quality assurance
Quality planning
B.why: An independent business function giving confidence that the project's quality controls are appropriate is quality assurance.

whyNot.0: Project assurance acts for the board inside the project.
whyNot.1: Quality control is the checking of products itself, done within the project.
whyNot.3: Quality planning sets specifications and produces product descriptions and the QMA.

C.q: Whose responsibility is project assurance, and of whom is it independent?
options: The business layer's; the whole project
The project board's; the project manager
The project manager's; the team managers
The senior supplier's; the users
C.why: Project assurance is the project board's responsibility and is independent of the project manager but not of the project.

whyNot.0: Independence from the whole project and a business home describe quality assurance.
whyNot.2: The PM cannot hold project assurance; it belongs to the board.
whyNot.3: Each board member is accountable for assurance of their own interest; it is not one supplier role.

C.q: In which management product is project assurance responsibility for quality recorded, and under which heading?
options: Quality register; result
Product description; composition
Project product description; acceptance criteria
Quality management approach; responsibilities
C.why: The responsibilities heading of the QMA covers quality planning and control responsibilities, including user, business and supplier project assurance.

whyNot.0: The result heading records whether a product passed or failed.
whyNot.2: Acceptance criteria describe what the project product must meet for acceptance.

C.q: A board member says, 'Our quality assurance is covered because Ruth provides business assurance for the board.' What is wrong with this?
options: Ruth's role is project assurance, not quality assurance
The executive must carry out business assurance personally
Quality assurance is the job of project support
Business assurance is not part of PRINCE2
C.why: Business assurance is a form of project assurance for the board; quality assurance is a separate function independent of the project management team.

whyNot.1: The executive is accountable for business assurance but may have others carry it out.
whyNot.2: Project support cannot provide assurance of any kind.
whyNot.3: Business, user and supplier assurance are the three areas of project assurance.

reteach.title: Restaurant kitchen checks
reteach.question: Who checks the kitchen, and for whom?

blocks.body: Chefs taste every dish before it leaves the pass: quality control. The owner asks a trusted manager to keep an eye on whether the kitchen is being run as agreed: that is like project assurance, acting for the people in charge. A food hygiene inspector from outside the restaurant checks that the kitchen's own checks are good enough: that is like quality assurance, independent of the whole team.

blocks.text: The owner's manager is inside the business of the restaurant; the inspector is not. Do not merge the two.

explain.body: A planned, systematic activity giving confidence that products will meet their specifications when tested under quality control.

options: Funding for the project's quality activities
Confidence that products will meet specifications
Approval of each finished product on delivery
A list of the products and their current status
test.why: Quality assurance provides confidence that products will meet their defined quality specifications when tested under quality control.

whyNot.0: Funding is secured by the executive.
whyNot.2: Approval of each product is defined in its product description's quality responsibilities.
whyNot.3: A list of products and their status is the product register.

explain.body: Quality assurance is a business or programme function managed outside the project management team.

test.q: Of whom is quality assurance independent?
options: The business layer
The programme
The project management team
The quality management system
test.why: Quality assurance is managed independently of the project management team.

whyNot.0: Quality assurance is typically a business function, so it is part of the business, not independent of it.
whyNot.1: Quality assurance may be performed at programme level, so it is not independent of the programme.
whyNot.3: Quality assurance may be performed by an element of the business's quality management system.

explain.body: The board's responsibility, confirming the project is conducted correctly; independent of the PM but part of the project.

options: The project manager
The project board
Project support
The business layer
test.why: Project assurance is the responsibility of the project board.

whyNot.0: Project assurance is independent of the project manager.
whyNot.2: Project support must be kept separate from assurance.
whyNot.3: The business layer commissions the project; project assurance belongs to the board.

explain.body: The project manager, project team members and project support cannot carry out project assurance.

test.q: Which person could the board appoint to provide user assurance?
options: The project manager
A developer in one of the project's teams
The project support officer
An experienced user from the business
test.why: The board may appoint people from the business to carry out project assurance; the PM, project team members and project support are excluded.

whyNot.0: Project assurance is independent of the project manager.
whyNot.1: Project team members, such as a developer, cannot carry out project assurance.
whyNot.2: Project support must be kept separate from assurance.
